Europe’s gas users brace for more pain this winter

Europe is facing another winter with exceptionally high gas prices thanks to the prolonged conflict between the United States and Iran and closure of the Strait of Hormuz, coming up top of the continued war between Russia and Ukraine.

EU gas storage facilities are less than two-thirds full, with only a few more weeks of the regular replenishment season to go before the heating season begins, which has sent prices climbing to the highest for over three years.

Storage facilities were filled to just 66% of their capacity on September 3, compared with an average of 83% on the same date in the last ten years, and the lowest in records dating back to 2011.

Low stocks will make weather-driven price spikes more likely and in the event more severe as the region scrambles to secure extra LNG from the spot market ...

Re: the ongoing debate about how much oil is getting through Hormuz and whether a particular WH claim is “True”, so so so much comes down to charity of the claim treatment and tone/framing of the assessment.

For example, a claim of 18 MMbbl over a given day can be an especially charitable clipped 24(ish) hour period—true in a tortured sense while misleading or cherry-picked.

Or a really high non-specific number can be charitably interpreted to mean the full broader middle east (with reroutes) rather than Hormuz, specifically.

Or a claim of 9 MMbpd when, say, only 6-7 MMbpd is confirmable can be both said to be “broadly” or “directionally” correct while at the same time being a “plausible exaggeration”. Or if that pace was only realized weeks after the claim it’s just “early.”

This is all fine! But given both the obvious fogginess of the data and the acute political undercurrent to the topic, best if folks are specific.

FWIW, I currently see Hormuz petroleum flows (crude + products) in the ballpark of 8 MMbpd**, with some of that representing re-displaced Saudi crude from the Red Sea.

And based on my tracking I have generally judged White House Hormuz transits numbers are directionally correct, plausible, but cherry-picked and often meant to mislead (like Trump’s 18 MMbbl claim).

**Chart below, highest I’ve confirmed thus far (with adjusted Kpler data) is just more than 8 MMbpd, with the current level lower but expected to be revised higher to roughly that same level.

There’s also the fact that the only way they’re managing to get this much oil through is thanks to enormous US military support, massive exporter discounts, ludicrously high insurance, etc.

#Agriculture:  The @UNFAO Food Price Index rose 1.9% in August, a third consecutive monthly gain, while the year-to-date increase remains a moderate 2.5%. All commodity groups recorded higher prices, led by sugar (+11.9% m/m, +7% y/y), dairy (+2.3% m/m, -19% y/y) and grains (+2.2% m/m, +10.9% y/y).

On the sugar surge, the FAO highlighted growing concerns over the 2026/27 global supply outlook. Hot and dry weather has reduced EU sugar beet yield forecasts, while El Niño-related conditions are threatening production across key Asian producers. Lower output in Brazil’s Center-South region and India’s announcement of duty-free raw sugar imports added to the tightening outlook.

International cereal prices also rose across all major grains in August, supported by strong demand, weather-related concerns over US and EU crop yields, robust feed and ethanol demand, and continued uncertainty over Black Sea exports.

Vegetable oils rose just 0.6% in August but remain the biggest contributor to food price gains over the past year, up 17.2%. Higher palm and soy oil prices outweighed weakness in sunflower and rapeseed oils, with palm supported by strong import demand and El Niño-related production concerns in Southeast Asia.

We're not frustrated, Secretary Wright. In this industry, we simply report our numbers in barrels per day over multiple days. Let's pick a date range and stick to it. No more "yesterday we shipped out 17 million barrels", thanks. And yes, we too see 9 Mbpd with crude & products.

The “returning tankers” are already in the GoO, but as we pointed out a couple of days ago, the dance floor is crowded. STS partners need to await their turn to dance. The port services which oversee those STS transfers, are stretched right now.

The Middle East oil landscape is undergoing a seismic shift. Crude oil exporting nations are establishing alternative routes to reduce the number of barrels sent through the SoH. Iraq is trucking more than 100 Kbpd to Syria to reach the Med Sea. The UAE is expected to double its pipeline capacity to the GoO sometime next year. Saudi Arabia already sends most of its crude oil exports via the Red Sea. Other countries are also exploring and developing alternative options.

Finally, a sensible figure. Unlike previous statements, this one is based on a daily average. We have 8 Mbpd of crude oil alone over the past seven complete days via the Strait of Hormuz; the rest is refined products.

Please note that we rarely use the term "oil" without specifying what kind. Most will state "oil" and also mean refined products such as gasoline, jet fuel and any other liquid fuels in addition to crude oil. We actually state "crude oil" when we mean just that and nothing else.
